source.title: The Constitution of India (original question writing)

chapter.name: Fundamental Rights: Your Claim Against the State
chapter.blurb: The idea and list of fundamental rights, equality, freedoms, rights against exploitation and of religion, constitutional remedies, and the limits and amendment of rights.

scope_in.item: Fundamental Rights, Articles 12 to 35, with the exceptions in Articles 31A-31C, the effect of an Emergency (Articles 358-359) and the amendability of rights
scope_in.pages: Laxmikanth Ch.8 pdf pages 127-169; Ch.12 pages 198-201; Ch.17 pages 262-264

scope_out.item: Points where other notes disagree with Laxmikanth or settled law (BCCI as State, Article 26(b) limits, year-only questions on judgments)

concepts.name: What fundamental rights are
concepts.description: The idea of enforceable rights against the State, where they sit in the Constitution and how a law that breaks them is treated.
concepts.idea: Fundamental rights are guarantees in Part III that a citizen can enforce in court against the State.
concepts.rule: Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) lists the fundamental rights. Article 12 says who counts as 'the State': the Union and State governments, Parliament and the legislatures, and local and other authorities. Article 13 makes any law that takes away or waters down these rights void to that extent. The rights are justiciable, so a person whose right is violated can go straight to the Supreme Court under Article 32. They are not absolute: the State may impose reasonable restrictions in the public interest. The right to property was removed from this list by the 44th Amendment (1978) and now survives as an ordinary legal right in Article 300A.
concepts.example: A person whose house is demolished by a municipal body without notice can question the action as an act of 'the State'.

questions.q: A writ petition alleges that an order passed by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation violated a fundamental right. The petition can be treated as one against 'the State' only if ONGC falls within Article 12. Under which limb of Article 12 does the chapter place bodies such as LIC, ONGC and SAIL?
questions.a: 'All other authorities', which covers statutory or non-statutory authorities
o: 'All other authorities', which covers statutory or non-statutory authorities
'Local authorities', since public-sector undertakings are an extension of municipal administration
'Government and legislature of states', since they are owned by public money through the Union and the states
None of the limbs, because Article 12 lists only governments, legislatures and local bodies, and no corporation
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.131) lists four limbs of Article 12: the Government and Parliament of India; the government and legislature of states; all local authorities (municipalities, panchayats, district boards, improvement trusts); and all other authorities, statutory or non-statutory, like LIC, ONGC and SAIL.
w: Local authorities are municipalities, panchayats, district boards and improvement trusts; the book places LIC, ONGC and SAIL under 'other authorities'.
That limb means the executive and legislative organs of a state government, not corporations.
Article 12 is deliberately wide so as to include all agencies of the State; corporations like ONGC are named by the book.

questions.q: A community follows a custom that has acquired the force of law, and the custom denies some members access to a village well. Whether the custom can be tested against the Fundamental Rights depends on the meaning of 'law' in Article 13. Which of the following is correct?
questions.a: It can be declared void to the extent it violates a fundamental right, because 'law' in Article 13 includes custom or usage having the force of law
o: It can be declared void to the extent it violates a fundamental right, because 'law' in Article 13 includes custom or usage having the force of law
It cannot be tested, because Article 13 covers only Acts passed by Parliament or by a state legislature, and a custom is not enacted by either body
It cannot be tested, because Article 13 covers legislation, ordinances and delegated rules but excludes any source that is not legislative in nature
It can be tested only by Parliament through an amending Act, since courts have no power to question a practice that has grown up through long usage
questions.e: Article 13 gives 'law' a wide meaning: permanent laws of Parliament and state legislatures, ordinances, delegated legislation (order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification) and non-legislative sources such as custom or usage having the force of law (Laxmikanth p.132). Any of these can be declared void for contravening Part III.
w: The chapter lists four kinds of 'law', and enacted statutes are only the first.
Ordinances and delegated rules are included, but so are non-legislative sources like custom having the force of law.
Courts, not Parliament, exercise the judicial review conferred by Article 13 through Articles 32 and 226.

questions.q: Which of the following was a Fundamental Right in the Constitution as originally adopted but is NOT listed among the six Fundamental Rights at present?
questions.e: The Constitution originally provided seven Fundamental Rights. The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 deleted the right to property (Article 31), making it a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII, so six remain (Laxmikanth p.127).
w: Articles 23 and 24 remain in Part III today.
Articles 29 and 30 remain in Part III today.
Article 32 remains in Part III today and is itself a fundamental right.

questions.q: According to the chapter, the rights in Part III are called 'fundamental' for two reasons. Which option states both of them?
questions.a: They are guaranteed and protected by the Constitution, the fundamental law of the land, and they are essential for the all-round development of the individual
o: They are guaranteed and protected by the Constitution, the fundamental law of the land, and they are essential for the all-round development of the individual
They cannot be amended by any procedure, and they are essential only for the political participation of citizens in the democratic life of the nation and its governance
They were borrowed from the Bill of Rights of the USA, and they are enforceable only against the executive and not against the legislature of the Union or the states
They are available to citizens alone, and they are enforceable by every court in the country on a petition from any aggrieved person, citizen or not
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.127): they are named so because the Constitution, the fundamental law of the land, guarantees and protects them; they are also fundamental because they are most essential for the all-round (material, intellectual, moral and spiritual) development of individuals.
w: Parliament can curtail or repeal them by a constitutional amendment, within the basic structure (p.129), so they are not unamendable.
US inspiration is true but it is not why they are called fundamental; they operate as limits on the legislature as well as the executive (p.127).
Some are available to all persons (p.130-131), and writ powers rest with the Supreme Court and High Courts, not every court (p.159).

questions.q: Article 13 is described as providing expressly for the doctrine of judicial review. Which courts exercise the power to declare a law void for contravening a fundamental right?
questions.a: The Supreme Court, acting through Article 32, together with the high courts, acting through Article 226
o: The Supreme Court, acting through Article 32, together with the high courts, acting through Article 226
The Supreme Court alone, under Article 32, with the high courts limited to ordinary legal rights
The Supreme Court under Article 32, and the high courts only on a reference made by the Supreme Court
Any court of civil or criminal jurisdiction, through its inherent power to test a statute before applying it
questions.e: Article 13 declares laws inconsistent with Part III void; this power of judicial review is conferred on the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the high courts (Article 226) (Laxmikanth p.132). Only these two classes of court can issue writs (p.159).
w: High courts under Article 226 can issue writs for fundamental rights as well as other purposes (p.160).
High courts have original writ power under Article 226; no reference from the Supreme Court is needed.
Only the Supreme Court and the high courts issue writs; Parliament has not empowered any other court (p.159).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the features of the Fundamental Rights:

1. Some of them are available only to citizens, while others are available to all persons.
2. Courts, and not the legislature, finally judge whether a restriction placed on a fundamental right is reasonable.
3. All of them are available only against State action, and none can be claimed against a private person.
4. Parliament can repeal them by an ordinary law, though it cannot alter the basic structure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 8.2 divides them into citizen-only rights and rights open to foreigners (except enemy aliens). Statement 2 is correct: The rights are qualified, not absolute; the State imposes restrictions but the courts judge reasonableness. Statement 3 is incorrect: Some, such as Article 15(2), Article 17 and Article 23, also operate against private individuals. Statement 4 is incorrect: They can be curtailed or repealed only by a constitutional amendment act, not an ordinary act.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights and the persons who can claim them:

1. The right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions under Article 30 is available only to citizens.
2. Freedom to manage religious affairs under Article 26 is available to foreigners, except enemy aliens, as well as to citizens.
3. Protection in respect of conviction for offences under Article 20 is available to citizens but not to foreigners.
4. Non-citizen children are outside Article 21A, which the chapter lists among the rights available only to citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 8.2 lists Article 30 among the rights available only to citizens (p.130). Statement 2 is correct: Table 8.2 lists Article 26 in the column open to both citizens and foreigners (p.130). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 20 is in the column open to both; the chapter says it protects an accused citizen, foreigner or legal person (pp.130, 147). Statement 4 is incorrect: Table 8.2 lists Article 21A in the column open to both citizens and foreigners (p.130).
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.130
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.130
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.130

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the definition of 'State' in Article 12:

1. It includes the executive and legislative organs of the Union government.
2. Panchayats and improvement trusts are outside the definition because they are not created by the Constitution.
3. Only authorities created by a statute fall under 'other authorities'; a non-statutory authority is outside Article 12.
4. An agency run by private persons stays outside 'State' under Article 12, however closely it acts as an instrument of the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Government and Parliament of India form the first limb. Statement 2 is incorrect: They are 'local authorities', expressly included along with municipalities and district boards. Statement 3 is incorrect: The book says 'other authorities' are statutory or non-statutory, like LIC, ONGC, SAIL. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Supreme Court has held that a private body or agency working as an instrument of the State falls within 'State'.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 13:

1. A bye-law, rule or notification issued under delegated power is 'law' for Article 13 and can be declared void if it conflicts with a fundamental right.
2. Article 13 itself declares that a constitutional amendment is a 'law' which can be struck down for violating Part III.
3. The Supreme Court and the high courts exercise the judicial review conferred by it.
4. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court held that a constitutional amendment can be challenged if it violates a fundamental right forming part of the basic structure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Statutory instruments in the nature of delegated legislation are listed as 'law' (p.132). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 13 declares that a constitutional amendment is not a law; only after Kesavananda can an amendment be challenged, and only on the basic structure (p.132). Statement 3 is correct: Through Article 32 and Article 226 respectively (p.132). Statement 4 is correct: The chapter records this exception to the rule that an amendment is not a law (p.132).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.132
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.132
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.132

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about constitutional rights located outside Part III:

1. Article 301, which keeps trade, commerce and intercourse free throughout India, is placed in Part III.
2. The bar on levying a tax except by authority of law, Article 265, lies in Part XII.
3. Adult suffrage as the basis of elections to the House of the People and the state assemblies is a constitutional right under Article 326, in Part XV.
4. For the infringement of these rights Article 32 cannot be invoked; the aggrieved person may go to the high court under Article 226 or file an ordinary suit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is in Part XIII, so it is a constitutional right outside Part III (p.168). Statement 2 is correct: Listed by the chapter among the rights outside Part III (p.168). Statement 3 is correct: A non-fundamental right listed on p.168. Statement 4 is correct: The chapter says the aggrieved person cannot avail the Article 32 remedy but can move the High Court by an ordinary suit or under Article 226 (p.168).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.168
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.168
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.168

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights in Part III:

1. The chapter says the Fundamental Rights prevent the establishment of an authoritarian and despotic rule by operating as limits on the executive and on arbitrary laws of the legislature.
2. The Fundamental Rights protect the liberties and freedoms of the people against invasion by the State.
3. The Fundamental Rights in our Constitution are less elaborate than those in the Constitution of the USA.
4. Part III extends from Article 12 to Article 35.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Stated in the opening of the chapter (p.127). Statement 2 is correct: Stated in the opening of the chapter (p.127). Statement 3 is incorrect: The book says they are more elaborate than those found in the Constitution of any other country, including the USA (p.127). Statement 4 is correct: The chapter begins with Articles 12 to 35 (p.127).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.127
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.127
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.127

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the general features of the Fundamental Rights:

1. An aggrieved person can go directly to the Supreme Court and need not come by way of appeal from a high court.
2. Parliament can curtail or repeal them only by a constitutional amendment act and not by an ordinary act.
3. Most are directly enforceable, while a few need a law for giving effect to them, which only Parliament can make under Article 35.
4. Some are negative in character, placing limits on the State, while others are positive, conferring privileges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: They are defended and guaranteed by the Supreme Court. Statement 2 is correct: And this must not affect the basic structure. Statement 3 is correct: Uniformity throughout the country is the reason. Statement 4 is correct: Both kinds are in Part III.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following criticisms of the Fundamental Rights recorded in the chapter:

1. Critics say that the judicial process is so expensive that the rights benefit mainly the rich section of society.
2. The list consists mainly of political rights and leaves out social and economic rights such as the right to work.
3. Sir Ivor Jennings's complaint was that the Fundamental Rights are based on no consistent philosophy.
4. The chapter records the criticism that the rights are too permanent, because Parliament cannot amend or abolish them.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Recorded under 'Expensive Remedy' (p.167). Statement 2 is correct: Recorded under 'No Social and Economic Rights' (p.167). Statement 3 is correct: Recorded under 'No Consistent Philosophy' (p.167). Statement 4 is incorrect: Under 'No Permanency' the critics say they are not sacrosanct: Parliament can curtail or abolish them, as it did with the right to property in 1978 (p.167).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.167
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.167
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.167

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights that can be claimed against private individuals:

1. A hotel owner, no less than the State, is bound by the rule in Article 15(2) against refusing access on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
2. Under Article 17, as read in the PUDR case (1982), a private person who practises untouchability is in breach of the guarantee.
3. Every Fundamental Right is available against the State; only some of them are available against private individuals as well.
4. Article 16(1), equality of opportunity in public employment, can be enforced against a private employer as well as against the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 15(2) bars discrimination in access to shops, hotels and similar places by private persons as well as the State (Laxmikanth p.134). Statement 2 is correct: in the PUDR case (1982) the Court held the Article 17 right available against private individuals, with the State bound to act to secure it (p.141). Statement 3 is correct: all Fundamental Rights lie against the State but only some also against private persons (p.129). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 16 deals with employment or office under the State (p.137), so it cannot be enforced against a private employer; it is not among the rights that reach private persons.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.134
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.134
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.134
tr: only some rights reach private persons

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the right to property:

1. After the 44th Amendment it can be regulated by an ordinary law of Parliament, without a constitutional amendment.
2. A person whose property right is violated can directly move the Supreme Court under Article 32.
3. According to the chapter, it is not a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is now only a legal right under Article 300-A. Statement 2 is incorrect: He can move the high court under Article 226, not Article 32. Statement 3 is correct: The book says so at the end of its discussion. So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the grouping of articles in Part III as given in the chapter:

1. Article 21A belongs to the group of rights titled Right to Freedom, Articles 19 to 22.
2. Safeguards for persons arrested or detained are the subject of Article 22.
3. The group of rights headed freedom of religion runs from Article 25 up to Article 28.
4. Article 18 forms part of the Right to Freedom.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 8.1 places Article 21A, elementary education, under the Right to Freedom, Articles 19-22 (Laxmikanth p.128). Statement 2 is correct: Article 22 is protection against arrest and detention in certain cases (p.128). Statement 3 is correct: the freedom of religion group runs from Article 25 to Article 28 (p.129). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 18, abolition of titles, belongs to the Right to Equality, Articles 14-18 (p.128). So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about compensation for acquisition of property:

1. Part III still carries a guaranteed right to compensation when the State acquires the property of a minority educational institution.
2. Article 31A requires compensation at market value when the State acquires land held under personal cultivation within the statutory ceiling.
3. Since the deletion of Article 31, Part III guarantees compensation whenever the State acquires any private property.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Added to Article 30 by the 44th Amendment Act (1978). Statement 2 is correct: This second compensation provision was added by the 17th Amendment Act (1964). Statement 3 is incorrect: Only the two cases above carry a guaranteed compensation; for others there is none. So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Fundamental Rights are justiciable.
Statement-II: In 1978 the 44th Amendment took the right to property out of Part III.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: persons can move the courts to enforce a violated Fundamental Right (Laxmikanth p.129). Statement-II is correct: the 44th Amendment (1978) moved property to Article 300-A (p.127). The removal of one right says nothing about why the rights are justiciable, so II does not explain I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is correct but it does not give the reason for Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; the 44th Amendment (1978) moved property to Article 300-A (p.127).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable in courts (p.129).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A registered company can invoke Article 14 against an action of the State, but it cannot claim the six freedoms of Article 19 in its own name.
Statement-II: Article 14 speaks of 'any person', which includes legal persons, whereas the rights in Article 19 are guaranteed to citizens.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct (Laxmikanth p.132: 'person' in Article 14 includes statutory corporations, companies and registered societies; p.142: the six rights are not available to legal persons like companies). Statement-II is correct and it is exactly the reason: the wording of Article 14 is 'person', that of Article 19 is 'citizens', so II explains I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; Article 14 says 'any person', which covers companies (p.132).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; a company can invoke Article 14 but not the six freedoms of Article 19 (pp.132, 142).

questions.q:
Match the Fundamental Right in List-I with the Article in List-II.

List-I
A. Freedom to manage religious affairs
B. Protection of language, script and culture of minorities
C. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
D. Immunity from being taxed to fund a particular religion

List-II
1. Article 23
2. Article 27
3. Article 26
4. Article 29
questions.e: Table 8.1 (Laxmikanth pp.128-129) lists freedom to manage religious affairs as Article 26, protection of language, script and culture of minorities as Article 29, prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour as Article 23, and freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any religion as Article 27.
w: 'A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2' swaps A and B: Article 26 is religious affairs and Article 29 is minority language and culture.
'A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1' swaps C and D: Article 23 is the ban on traffic in human beings and Article 27 is freedom from taxes for promoting a religion.
'A-1, B-4, C-3, D-2' swaps A and C: Article 26 is religious affairs and Article 23 is the ban on traffic in human beings.
tr: look-alike article numbers in Part III

concepts.name: Equality before the law
concepts.description: Articles 14 to 18: equal protection, no discrimination, equal opportunity in public jobs, ending untouchability and titles.
concepts.idea: The State must treat people alike and cannot use birth or status to give some people advantage.
concepts.rule: Article 14 promises equality before the law and equal protection of the laws. Article 15 forbids discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, though special provisions for women, children and weaker sections are allowed. Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment, with provision for reservation. Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its practice punishable. Article 18 abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions, and stops a citizen from accepting titles from a foreign State.
concepts.example: A government job advertisement cannot be limited to men of one caste without a permitted reason.

questions.q: Article 14 joins two ideas of different origin. In the chapter's account, which of the following correctly pairs each idea with its nature?
questions.a: The idea of British origin says no one is above the ordinary law and is negative; the idea of American origin says likes must be treated alike and is positive
o: The idea of British origin says no one is above the ordinary law and is negative; the idea of American origin says likes must be treated alike and is positive
The idea of American origin says no one is above the ordinary law and is negative; the idea of British origin says likes must be treated alike and is positive
The idea of British origin says likes must be treated alike and is negative; the idea of American origin says no one is above the ordinary law and is positive
Both ideas say that no one is above the ordinary law and both are negative; they differ only in that one is of British and the other of American origin
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.132): equality before law (British) means absence of special privileges and equal subjection to the ordinary law, a negative concept; equal protection of the laws (American) means equal treatment in equal circumstances, a positive concept.
w: The origins are swapped.
Natures and tasks are swapped between the two ideas.
The two ideas differ in content: the American one is about like treatment of those similarly situated, and is positive.

questions.q: A state law, reserved for the President and assented to by him, is enacted to implement the policy in clause (b) of Article 39 and is challenged in court as violating Article 14. According to the chapter, what is the position?
questions.a: The challenge fails on that ground, because Article 31-C shields such laws from Article 14: 'where Article 31-C comes in, Article 14 goes out'
o: The challenge fails on that ground, because Article 31-C shields such laws from Article 14: 'where Article 31-C comes in, Article 14 goes out'
The challenge succeeds, because Article 14 is a basic feature and no law, whether made by Parliament or a state, can be exempted from it by any Article
The challenge succeeds unless the law has also been placed in the Ninth Schedule, which alone can shield a law from Article 14 under Article 31-B
The challenge fails only if the law was passed by Parliament itself, since a state law cannot enjoy any exemption from Article 14
questions.e: Article 31-C is an exception to Article 14: laws made by the state for implementing the Directive Principles in Article 39(b) or (c) cannot be challenged as violating Article 14. The Supreme Court said 'where Article 31-C comes in, Article 14 goes out' (Laxmikanth pp.133-134).
w: The chapter lists Article 31-C as an exception to equality for Article 39(b) and (c) laws.
The protection comes from Article 31-C, not from the Ninth Schedule (Article 31-B).
The chapter speaks of laws made by the state for implementing the directive principles; it does not limit the exception to Parliament.

questions.q: In Balaji Raghavan (1995) the Supreme Court dealt with the Bharat Ratna and Padma awards. Which of the following did it hold?
questions.a: The awards are valid and are not 'titles', but must not be used as prefixes or suffixes to names, failing which the awardee forfeits the award
o: The awards are valid and are not 'titles', but must not be used as prefixes or suffixes to names, failing which the awardee forfeits the award
The awards violate Article 18 because they confer a distinction on citizens, and they must be discontinued except for military and academic awards given by the State
The awards are valid, and awardees may freely use them as prefixes or suffixes to their names since the awards are not titles of nobility within Article 18
The awards are valid only if the President consents to each conferment, as a foreign State or its citizens may be involved in such awards under Article 18
questions.e: The Court upheld the awards: Article 18 prohibits only hereditary titles of nobility, and equality does not mean merit cannot be recognised. But it ruled they should not be used as suffixes or prefixes, or the awardee forfeits the award (Laxmikanth p.141).
w: Article 18 bars only hereditary titles of nobility; the Court did not strike down the awards.
The Court expressly barred use as prefix or suffix.
Presidential consent is the rule for gifts and offices from foreign States, not for the national awards.

questions.q: A 1955 statute giving effect to Article 17 was comprehensively amended in 1976 to enlarge its scope and make its penal provisions more stringent. Which statement about it is correct?
questions.a: It became the Protection of Civil Rights Act, which defines 'civil right' but, like the Constitution, does not define untouchability
o: It became the Protection of Civil Rights Act, which defines 'civil right' but, like the Constitution, does not define untouchability
It became the Untouchability (Offences) Act, which defines untouchability as the social disabilities imposed on certain classes of persons by reason of their birth in certain castes
It became the Protection of Civil Rights Act, which defines untouchability as the practice as it had developed historically in the country over many centuries
It was repealed and replaced in 1976 by a new Act that extended the prohibition of Article 17 to private persons alone and not to the State itself
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.141: the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was amended and renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 in 1976; it defines 'civil right' but neither it nor the Constitution defines 'untouchability'.
w: The Untouchability (Offences) Act was the old name; the new name is Protection of Civil Rights Act, and untouchability is not defined.
The 'historical practice' reading comes from the Mysore High Court, not from a definition in the Act.
The Act was amended and renamed, not repealed, and Article 17 operates against the State and private persons alike.

questions.q: The Second Backward Classes Commission, whose report led to the 27 per cent job reservation for OBCs, was appointed under which provision, and by which government?
questions.e: The Morarji Desai Government appointed the Mandal Commission in 1979 under Article 340; it reported in 1980 and recommended 27% reservation. The V.P. Singh Government announced the 27% reservation in 1990 (Laxmikanth p.139).
w: V.P. Singh's government implemented the report in 1990; it did not appoint the commission.
Article 16(4) permits reservation; the commission was set up under Article 340.
Article 338-B was inserted in 2018; the Narasimha Rao government made changes in 1991 but did not appoint the commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 14:

1. The word 'person' in Article 14 covers citizens only and excludes companies and corporations.
2. Where equals and unequals are treated differently, Article 14 does not apply.
3. It forbids class legislation but permits reasonable classification of persons, objects and transactions.
4. A classification is valid even if it is arbitrary or artificial, provided the law is passed by Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It covers all persons, citizens or foreigners, and legal persons like companies. Statement 2 is correct: The Supreme Court said so; the protection is against unlike treatment of likes. Statement 3 is correct: The classification must rest on an intelligible differential and substantial distinction. Statement 4 is incorrect: Classification should not be arbitrary, artificial or evasive.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about equality before the law and its exceptions, as discussed in the chapter:

1. A.V. Dicey's concept of the Rule of Law has three elements: absence of arbitrary power, equality before the law, and primacy of the rights of the individual.
2. Equality before law admits an exception for foreign sovereigns, ambassadors and diplomats, who cannot be tried in Indian courts for crimes or sued in civil cases.
3. The Supreme Court held that the Rule of Law embodied in Article 14 is a basic feature, but one that Parliament may remove by a constitutional amendment.
4. The United Nations and its agencies, not being sovereign States, enjoy no diplomatic immunity in India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: These are the three aspects listed (p.133). Statement 2 is correct: Listed among the exceptions to equality (p.134). Statement 3 is incorrect: A basic feature cannot be destroyed even by an amendment (p.133). Statement 4 is incorrect: The chapter lists the UNO and its agencies as enjoying diplomatic immunity (p.134).
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.133
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.133
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.133

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the immunities of the President and the Governors under Article 361:

1. They are answerable to the courts for the exercise of the powers of the office, though not for personal acts.
2. During the term of office, a court can neither start nor carry on a criminal case against them.
3. No court may order the arrest or imprisonment of either of them while in office.
4. A civil proceeding for an act done in a personal capacity may be instituted during the term only after two months have passed since notice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: They are not answerable to any court for exercise and performance of the powers and duties of the office. Statement 2 is correct: Stated in Article 361 as described. Statement 3 is correct: Part of the same immunity. Statement 4 is correct: This covers acts before or after entering office.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 15 and the amendments relating to it:

1. The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 provides a 27 per cent quota for OBC candidates in the central higher educational institutions it covers.
2. Article 15(5) was added by the 93rd Amendment Act, 2005, and covers private educational institutions, aided or unaided, except minority institutions.
3. Article 15(6), allowing up to 10 per cent reservation for economically weaker sections, was added by the 102nd Amendment Act.
4. Article 15(3), allowing special provision for women and children, was inserted by the 93rd Amendment Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Act gives effect to Article 15(5) with a 27 per cent OBC quota in the central higher educational institutions it covers; the Court upheld it in 2008 but directed exclusion of the creamy layer (Laxmikanth pp.134-135). Statement 2 is correct: Table 8.3 records clause (5), added by the 93rd Amendment Act, 2005, covering aided and unaided private educational institutions other than minority institutions (p.135). Statement 3 is incorrect: clause (6), the 10 per cent reservation for economically weaker sections, was added by the 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 (p.135). Statement 4 is incorrect: clause (3), special provision for women and children, is an original clause; the 93rd Amendment inserted clause (5) (p.135).
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.134
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.134
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.134

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the non-discrimination provisions of Article 15:

1. Article 15(1) protects every person, whether a citizen or a foreigner, from discrimination by the State on the listed grounds.
2. The first provision of Article 15 operates against the State alone, and 'discrimination' in it means to distinguish unfavourably from others.
3. The State may make special provision for women and children without breaching the Article.
4. Public wells, tanks, bathing ghats and roads, if kept up wholly or partly from State funds or opened to the public, fall within the non-discrimination guarantee of Article 15(2).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 15 speaks of 'any citizen' and Table 8.2 lists it among the citizen-only rights (pp.130, 134). Statement 2 is correct: As explained in the chapter (p.134). Statement 3 is correct: The first of the four exceptions (p.134). Statement 4 is correct: As described under the second provision (p.134).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.130
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.130
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.130

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic criteria for reservation as given in the chapter:

1. According to the chapter, the gross annual income ceiling of the OBC creamy layer was raised to Rs 8 lakh in 2017.
2. When the creamy layer ceiling was introduced in 1993 it was Rs 2.5 lakh.
3. Under the 2019 order described in the chapter, a family is identified as EWS if its gross annual income from all sources, for the financial year before the application, is below Rs 8 lakh.
4. Under that order, a family owning a residential flat of 1,000 sq ft or more is excluded from the EWS category irrespective of its income.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The chapter lists revisions in 2004, 2008, 2013 and 2017 (p.136). Statement 2 is incorrect: It was Rs 1 lakh in 1993; Rs 2.5 lakh came in 2004 (p.136). Statement 3 is correct: The income test under the order (p.136). Statement 4 is correct: One of the asset tests listed (p.136).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.136
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.136
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.136

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 16:

1. Article 16(2) lists descent and residence among the grounds, in addition to religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth.
2. Article 16(4A) on reservation in promotion for SCs and STs was added by the 77th Amendment (1995), and the 85th Amendment (2001) added consequential seniority.
3. Article 16(4B) lets the State treat unfilled reserved vacancies of a year as a separate class, outside the 50 per cent ceiling of that year; it was added by the 81st Amendment Act (2000).
4. Article 16(5) allows a law to require that the incumbent of a religious institution's office belong to that religion or denomination.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 16(2) names descent and residence in addition to religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth, whereas Article 15 does not list descent or residence (Laxmikanth p.137). Statement 2 is correct: Table 8.4 records clause (4A), reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, added by the 77th Amendment (1995), with consequential seniority added by the 85th Amendment (2001) (pp.137-138). Statement 3 is correct: clause (4B), added by the 81st Amendment (2000), lets unfilled reserved vacancies of a year be treated as a separate class outside that year's 50 per cent ceiling (Table 8.4). Statement 4 is correct: clause (5) permits a law requiring the holder of an office of a religious institution to belong to that religion or denomination (Table 8.4).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.137
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.137
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.137

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the developments after the Mandal Commission, as recorded in the chapter:

1. In 1991 the Narasimha Rao Government gave preference to the poorer sections among the OBCs within the 27 per cent quota and reserved a further 10 per cent of jobs for other economically backward sections.
2. Although it upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota in Indra Sawhney, the Supreme Court struck down the extra 10 per cent reservation for other economically backward sections.
3. The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs so that total reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs would amount to 50 per cent.
4. The Ram Nandan Committee recommended that reservation be extended to promotions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The two changes of 1991 (p.139). Statement 2 is correct: While upholding the 27 per cent OBC quota with conditions (p.139). Statement 3 is correct: Stated in the account of the Commission's report (p.139). Statement 4 is incorrect: It was appointed to identify the creamy layer among the OBCs (p.139).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.139
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.139
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.139

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 17:

1. Article 17 forbids the practice of untouchability in any form, and a disability arising out of it is punishable as an offence under law.
2. Social boycott of a few individuals is covered by Article 17, according to the Mysore High Court.
3. The Constitution defines 'untouchability' as the social disabilities imposed on persons by birth in certain castes.
4. In the PUDR case the Court placed the State under a constitutional duty to act so that the Article 17 right is not infringed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 17 as described (p.140). Statement 2 is incorrect: The Court held it does not cover social boycott of a few individuals or exclusion from religious services (p.141). Statement 3 is incorrect: The term is defined neither in the Constitution nor in the Act (p.141). Statement 4 is correct: People's Union for Democratic Rights case (1982), p.141.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.140
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.140
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.140

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indra Sawhney (Mandal) case, 1992:

1. The Court upheld the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, subject to excluding the creamy layer.
2. The Court held that there should be no reservation in promotions and that existing ones could continue for five years only.
3. Fifty per cent was fixed as the general ceiling on reserved posts, to be applied afresh each year, with room only for extraordinary situations.
4. The Court held the carry-forward rule for unfilled vacancies invalid, even if the 50 per cent limit is respected.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A condition of validity. Statement 2 is correct: That is, until 1997. Statement 3 is correct: Third condition. Statement 4 is incorrect: It held the carry-forward rule valid, provided it does not violate the 50 per cent rule. So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 18, as the chapter presents it:

1. Titles such as Maharaja, Rai Saheb and Dewan Bahadur, which colonial States conferred, fall under the ban in Article 18 as hereditary titles of nobility.
2. A citizen of India who holds no office of profit under the State is free to accept a title from a foreign State.
3. For a foreigner holding an office of profit or trust, the President's consent is needed for accepting a title but not for a present or emolument from a foreign State.
4. Article 18 allows the State to confer a military or an academic distinction even though it bars other titles.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the chapter says the hereditary titles of nobility conferred by colonial States, such as Maharaja, Raj Bahadur, Rai Bahadur, Rai Saheb and Dewan Bahadur, are banned by Article 18 (Laxmikanth p.141). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 18 prohibits a citizen of India from accepting any title from any foreign State, whatever his employment (p.141). Statement 3 is incorrect: the President's consent is needed for the present, emolument or office from a foreign State as well (p.141). Statement 4 is correct: the State is barred from conferring titles except a military or academic distinction (p.141). So exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: statement 4 is also correct, so the correct statements are 1 and 4.
'All four' miscounts: statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.
'None' miscounts: statements 1 and 4 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Awards:

1. They were instituted in 1954 and discontinued in 1977 by the Janata Party government headed by Morarji Desai.
2. The Padma Awards are announced on Republic Day, with brief interruptions in 1978-79 and 1993-97.
3. The chapter's ceiling of 120 Padma Awards a year counts posthumous awards and awards to NRIs, foreigners and OCIs.
4. They were revived in 1980 by the Indira Gandhi government.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the National Awards were instituted in 1954 and discontinued in 1977 by the Janata Party government headed by Morarji Desai (Laxmikanth p.141). Statement 2 is correct: the Padma Awards are announced on Republic Day, apart from interruptions in 1978-79 and 1993-97 (p.141). Statement 3 is incorrect: the ceiling of 120 excludes posthumous awards and awards to NRIs, foreigners and OCIs (p.141). Statement 4 is correct: the awards were revived in 1980 by the Indira Gandhi government (p.141). So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Members of Parliament cannot be proceeded against in a court for any vote they give in the House.
Statement-II: A substantially true report, published without malice, of the proceedings of either House of Parliament cannot give rise to civil or criminal liability for a newspaper.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct (Article 105, Laxmikanth p.133). Statement-II is correct: Article 361-A protects a substantially true report of the proceedings of either House (the chapter states the protection; the Article's proviso leaves out publication made with malice). Both are exceptions to equality before law, but the press protection is not the reason for a member's immunity, so II does not explain I.
w: Rejected: the member's immunity rests on Article 105 (privilege of the House), not on the protection given to the press.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; Article 361-A protects a substantially true report of House proceedings.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; Article 105 shields a member from court action over votes given in Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The primacy of the rights of the individual, Dicey's third element of the Rule of Law, applies to the Indian system as fully as the first two elements do.
Statement-II: In the Indian system the Constitution itself is the source of the individual rights.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: the chapter says Dicey's third element, the primacy of individual rights as a result of court decisions, does not apply to India (Laxmikanth p.133). Statement-II is correct: in India the Constitution itself is the source of the individual rights, which is why the third element does not fit.
w: Rejected: Statement-I is incorrect (the chapter says Dicey's third element does not apply to India), so the pair cannot both be correct with an explanation.
Rejected: Statement-I is incorrect, so there is no pair of correct statements, whatever the link between them.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (the Constitution itself is the source of individual rights), so calling it incorrect fails.

questions.q:
Match each institution or ruling in List-I with what it did, as recorded in the chapter, in List-II.

List-I
A. Mandal Commission
B. Ram Nandan Committee
C. National Commission for Backward Classes (1993)
D. Balaji Raghavan case

List-II
1. Identified 3743 castes as socially and educationally backward
2. Examines complaints of over-inclusion and under-inclusion in the OBC list
3. Held that the national awards are not titles under Article 18
4. Identified the creamy layer among the OBCs
questions.e: Mandal Commission identified 3743 castes (p.139); Ram Nandan Committee identified the creamy layer (p.139); NCBC (1993) examines complaints of over- and under-inclusion (p.139); Balaji Raghavan held the awards are not titles (p.141).
w: 'A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3' mismatches A, B: Mandal Commission identified 3743 castes (p.139); Ram Nandan Committee identified the creamy layer (p.139); NCBC (1993) examines complaints of over- and under-inclusion (p.139); Balaji Raghavan held the awards are not titles (p.141).

'A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3' mismatches B, C: Mandal Commission identified 3743 castes (p.139); Ram Nandan Committee identified the creamy layer (p.139); NCBC (1993) examines complaints of over- and under-inclusion (p.139); Balaji Raghavan held the awards are not titles (p.141).

'A-1, B-4, C-3, D-2' mismatches C, D: Mandal Commission identified 3743 castes (p.139); Ram Nandan Committee identified the creamy layer (p.139); NCBC (1993) examines complaints of over- and under-inclusion (p.139); Balaji Raghavan held the awards are not titles (p.141).

concepts.name: Freedoms and protection of life and liberty
concepts.description: Articles 19 to 22: the six freedoms, safeguards for accused persons, the right to life and personal liberty, education and arrest.
concepts.idea: Citizens enjoy specific freedoms, and life, liberty and fair procedure are protected against arbitrary State action.
concepts.rule: Article 19(1) gives citizens six freedoms: speech and expression; assembling peaceably without arms; forming associations, unions or cooperative societies; moving freely throughout India; residing and settling in any part; and practising any profession or carrying on any trade. Each can be limited by reasonable restrictions. Article 20 protects an accused against a law applied backwards, against being punished twice for the same offence and against being forced to testify against oneself. Article 21 says no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law. Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002) makes education free and compulsory for children aged 6 to 14. Article 22 gives safeguards on arrest, including being told the grounds and being produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
concepts.example: A person arrested must be taken before a magistrate within 24 hours, excluding travel time.

questions.q: Parliament enacts a law imposing a tax on income earned in an earlier year, which the earlier law did not tax. The law is challenged under Article 20(1). According to the chapter, what is the position?
questions.a: The challenge fails, because the bar on ex-post-facto laws applies only to criminal laws and not to civil or tax laws
o: The challenge fails, because the bar on ex-post-facto laws applies only to criminal laws and not to civil or tax laws
The challenge succeeds, because Article 20(1) bars every retrospective law, whether criminal, civil or fiscal
The challenge succeeds, because a tax is a penalty and Article 20(1) forbids a greater penalty than the law then in force
The challenge fails only if the law is passed during a national emergency, when Article 20 is suspended
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.147): Article 20(1)'s limit on retrospective laws is imposed only on criminal laws and not on civil or tax laws, so a civil liability or a tax can be imposed retrospectively. Also, Article 20 cannot be suspended in an emergency (p.131).
w: The protection is confined to criminal laws.
The chapter distinguishes tax from penalty; tax laws are outside Article 20(1).
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during a National Emergency; the challenge fails for the reason above, not because of an emergency.

questions.q: A law prescribes a procedure for depriving a person of personal liberty which a court finds arbitrary and oppressive, though the procedure is duly enacted. Under the Supreme Court's reading of Article 21 in the Maneka Gandhi case (1978), the law is
questions.a: open to being struck down, since the procedure must be reasonable, fair and just and conform to natural justice
o: open to being struck down, since the procedure must be reasonable, fair and just and conform to natural justice
valid, because Article 21 requires only a procedure established by law and the courts cannot examine whether it is just
valid, because the protection of Article 21 is available only against arbitrary executive action and not legislative action
invalid only if it deprives a citizen, because Article 21 does not protect non-citizens against legislation
questions.e: In Gopalan (1950) the Court held that Article 21 protects only against executive action and that a law's procedure could not be questioned as unfair. Maneka (1978) overruled it: the procedure must be reasonable, fair and just, so Article 21 operates against arbitrary legislative action too (Laxmikanth p.148).
w: That was the Gopalan position, overruled in Maneka.
That is also the Gopalan view; Maneka extended protection to arbitrary legislative action.
Article 21 is available to citizens and non-citizens alike (p.147).

questions.q: The State starts a trade as a complete monopoly, shutting out private citizens, and a trader claims violation of Article 19(1)(g). According to the chapter,
questions.a: no objection can be made, since the State may carry on any trade to the exclusion of citizens and need not justify its monopoly
o: no objection can be made, since the State may carry on any trade to the exclusion of citizens and need not justify its monopoly
the monopoly is valid only if the State shows that it serves the interests of the general public, as with any other restriction on the freedom
the monopoly is valid only if it is partial, since a complete exclusion of citizens would destroy the freedom guaranteed by Article 19(1)(g)
the monopoly is valid only if Parliament enacts it, since a state government cannot shut out citizens from a trade or business
questions.e: Article 19(6) lets the State carry on any trade, business, industry or service, wholly or partly to the exclusion of citizens or in competition with them; the State is not required to justify its monopoly (Laxmikanth p.146).
w: The State is not required to justify its monopoly.
The exclusion may be complete or partial.
The chapter does not limit the power to Parliament.

questions.q: According to the chapter (8th edition), which of the following is correct about the advisory board in a case of preventive detention under the second part of Article 22?
questions.a: It consists of judges of a high court, and Parliament is authorised to prescribe the procedure to be followed by it in an enquiry
o: It consists of judges of a high court, and Parliament is authorised to prescribe the procedure to be followed by it in an enquiry
It consists of judges of the Supreme Court, and each state legislature prescribes the procedure to be followed by it in an enquiry
It consists of judges of a high court, and its opinion is required for every detention, however short, under a preventive detention law
It consists of the district magistrate and two senior police officers, and its procedure is fixed by the Constitution itself
questions.e: Article 22 provides that a detention beyond three months needs the report of an advisory board consisting of judges of a high court, and it authorises Parliament to prescribe the circumstances in which detention may exceed three months without the board's opinion, the maximum period of detention, and the procedure to be followed by the board in an enquiry (Laxmikanth p.152).
w: The board consists of high court judges, and the procedure is a matter for Parliament, not the state legislatures.
The board's report is needed only when detention is to go beyond three months, unless Parliament has prescribed otherwise.
The board is made up of high court judges; the Constitution leaves the procedure to a law of Parliament.

questions.q: In which sequence of judgments did the Supreme Court first recognise a right to education up to any level including professional education, and later confine the right to free education until the age of 14?
questions.a: Mohini Jain (1992), later overruled by Unni Krishnan (1993)
o: Mohini Jain (1992), later overruled by Unni Krishnan (1993)
Unni Krishnan (1993), later overruled by Mohini Jain (1992)
Mohini Jain (1992), which was affirmed by Unni Krishnan (1993)
Unni Krishnan (1993), which was followed by the 86th Amendment of 2002 overruling the judgment
questions.e: In Mohini Jain (1992) the Court partly declared a fundamental right to education up to any level including medicine and engineering. In Unni Krishnan (1993) it overruled this: every child has a right to free education until 14, after which the right is subject to the economic capacity and development of the State (Laxmikanth p.150).
w: Mohini Jain came first (1992), and Unni Krishnan (1993) overruled it.
Unni Krishnan overruled Mohini Jain; it did not affirm it.
The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A; it did not overrule any judgment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the restrictions the State may place on the freedoms of Article 19:

1. Morality is a ground on which the freedom of assembly may be restricted under Article 19(3).
2. Protection of the interests of any scheduled tribe is a ground for restricting both the freedom of movement and the freedom of residence.
3. Decency or morality was added as a ground on speech by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951.
4. Contempt of court and defamation are among the grounds on which speech can be restricted.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Table 8.5 allows restriction of assembly on grounds of sovereignty and integrity of India and public order; morality is a ground for restricting association, not assembly (Laxmikanth pp.143-145). Statement 2 is correct: the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe is a ground under Article 19(5) for restricting both movement and residence (pp.145-146). Statement 3 is incorrect: decency or morality is among the original grounds of Article 19(2); the Table does not mark it as added by the 1st Amendment (p.143). Statement 4 is correct: contempt of court and defamation are among the Article 19(2) grounds on speech (p.143).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.143
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.143
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.143

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the freedom of speech and expression:

1. The Supreme Court has held that it includes the freedom of the press.
2. It includes the right against a bundh called by a political party or organisation.
3. It includes a right to strike.
4. It includes the right to know about government activities.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: In the list of what it includes. Statement 2 is correct: Also in the list. Statement 3 is incorrect: It includes demonstration or picketing but not the right to strike. Statement 4 is correct: Listed.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the freedoms of assembly and association:

1. The freedom of association includes the negative right not to form or join an association.
2. Official recognition of an association is itself guaranteed as a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c).
3. The right to form an association includes the right to continue with it, and not merely to start it.
4. The guarantee of assembly does not protect an assembly that is violent or involves arms.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the freedom of association includes the negative right not to form or join an association (Laxmikanth p.145). Statement 2 is incorrect: the chapter says the right to obtain recognition of an association is not a fundamental right (p.145). Statement 3 is correct: the right to form an association includes the right to continue with it (p.145). Statement 4 is correct: the guarantee protects only peaceable and unarmed assemblies, so a violent or armed one is outside it (p.145).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.145
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.145
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.145

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the freedoms of movement, residence and profession:

1. Article 19 protects only the internal dimension of movement; the right to travel abroad flows from Article 21.
2. 'Settle' in Article 19(1)(e) refers to a temporary stay, while 'reside' means making a permanent home.
3. The Bombay High Court struck down the restrictions on the movement of persons affected by AIDS.
4. In the Anuradha Bhasin case (2020) the Supreme Court held that trade over the internet is protected by Article 19(1)(g), and restrictions must satisfy proportionality.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Chapter says the external dimension is dealt with by Article 21. Statement 2 is incorrect: It is the other way round: reside is temporary stay, settle is permanent domicile. Statement 3 is incorrect: It validated them. Statement 4 is correct: It also held indefinite suspension of internet services impermissible.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the protections under Article 20:

1. The bar on ex-post-facto laws also forbids the trial of a person under a retrospective criminal law.
2. The bar on double jeopardy applies where a person has been both prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
3. The protection under Article 20 is available to a citizen, a foreigner and a legal person like a company.
4. The immunity against ex-post-facto laws cannot be claimed in the case of preventive detention.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It prohibits only conviction or sentence under such a law and not the trial (p.147). Statement 2 is correct: Article 20(2) as described (p.147). Statement 3 is correct: It is for an accused person (p.147). Statement 4 is correct: Stated in the chapter (p.147).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.147
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.147
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.147

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court cases through which rights were read into Article 21, as listed in Table 8.6 of the chapter:

1. Olga Tellis (1985) and Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra (1985) were decided in the same year.
2. Common Cause (2018) was decided after K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).
3. Hussainara Khatoon (1979), the case for the right to speedy trial, was decided after the Maneka Gandhi judgment of 1978.
4. Shantistar Builders (1990), the case for the right to shelter, was decided after Parmanand Katara (1989).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 8.6 dates Olga Tellis and Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra both to 1985 (Laxmikanth p.151). Statement 2 is correct: Puttaswamy is 2017 and Common Cause 2018, so the latter came later (p.151). Statement 3 is correct: Maneka Gandhi is 1978 (p.148) and Hussainara Khatoon, the speedy trial case, 1979 (p.150). Statement 4 is correct: Parmanand Katara is 1989 and Shantistar Builders, the right to shelter, 1990 (p.151).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.151
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.151
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.151

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cases expanding Article 21:

1. Satwant Singh Sawhney (1967) declared the right to speedy trial.
2. Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) declared the right of a prisoner to have the necessities of life.
3. Olga Tellis (1985) declared the right to livelihood.
4. K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) declared the right to privacy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Satwant Singh Sawhney (1967) concerned the right to travel abroad; the right to speedy trial came in Hussainara Khatoon (1979) (Laxmikanth pp.149-150). Statement 2 is correct: Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) is recorded for the prisoner's right to the necessities of life (Table 8.6, p.151). Statement 3 is correct: Olga Tellis (1985) is recorded for the right to livelihood (p.151). Statement 4 is correct: K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) is recorded for the right to privacy (p.151).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.149
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.149
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.149

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about arrest and detention under Article 22:

1. A person arrested under an ordinary law has the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest.
2. An arrested person must be brought before a magistrate within two days, the journey time not counted.
3. A person arrested under an ordinary law may consult a lawyer and be defended by him.
4. The first part of Article 22 covers arrest under the orders of a court and civil arrest.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: First part of Article 22 (p.152). Statement 2 is incorrect: The period is 24 hours, excluding the journey time (p.152). Statement 3 is correct: First part of Article 22 (p.152). Statement 4 is incorrect: The Supreme Court ruled that it does not cover these (p.152).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.152
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.152
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.152

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about preventive detention in the chapter:

1. Preventive detention for reasons of defence, foreign affairs or the security of India is a matter on which only Parliament can legislate.
2. The protection given by the second part of Article 22 is available to citizens but not to aliens.
3. A person held under a preventive detention order must be given a chance to represent against it.
4. A detenu must be told why he is held, save for facts whose disclosure the public interest forbids.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Division of legislative power (p.152). Statement 2 is incorrect: It is available to both citizens and aliens (p.152). Statement 3 is correct: A safeguard in the second part (p.152). Statement 4 is correct: Stated in the chapter (p.152).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.152
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.152
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.152

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the right to education:

1. Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 and makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged six to fourteen.
2. The 86th Amendment changed Article 45 in Part IV so that it now directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for children until they complete six years of age.
3. The 86th Amendment of 2002 and the RTE Act of 2009 both took effect from 1 April 2010.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: As the State may determine (p.150). Statement 2 is correct: Stated in the chapter (p.150). Statement 3 is correct: w.e.f. 1 April 2010 (p.151). So exactly 3 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about statutes enacted by Parliament on preventive detention:

1. The Preventive Detention Act of 1950 lapsed in 1969.
2. MISA (1971) stayed on the statute book until 1977.
3. TADA (1985) remained in force until 1999.
4. POTA, enacted in 2002, was repealed two years later.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: As per the list. Statement 2 is incorrect: It was repealed in 1978. Statement 3 is incorrect: It was repealed in 1995. Statement 4 is correct: As per the list. So exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'Only three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the six freedoms of Article 19:

1. Article 19 once guaranteed seven freedoms; the 44th Amendment of 1978 removed the freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
2. The six rights are protected against State action and are available to citizens and to shareholders of a company, but not to foreigners or companies as such.
3. The State may impose reasonable restrictions on them on any ground Parliament considers necessary in the public interest.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Property was in 19(1)(f). Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 3 is incorrect: Only on the grounds mentioned in Article 19 itself and not on any other grounds. So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A person may be compelled by the police to give a blood specimen without breaching the protection against self-incrimination.
Statement-II: According to the chapter, the protection against self-incrimination extends to civil proceedings as well as criminal proceedings.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: compulsory blood specimens, thumb impressions, specimen signatures and exhibition of the body are outside the protection of Article 20(3) (Laxmikanth p.147).
