Statement-II is incorrect: the chapter says the protection extends only to criminal proceedings and not to civil proceedings or proceedings which are not of a criminal nature (p.147).
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so there is no explanation to judge; the chapter limits the protection to criminal proceedings.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect as the chapter puts it (p.147), so the pair cannot both be correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; a blood specimen is outside the protection (p.147), and it is Statement-II that fails.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: After the Maneka Gandhi case, a law depriving a person of personal liberty can be struck down as arbitrary legislative action.
Statement-II: The Maneka judgment required that the procedure prescribed by a law depriving a person of life or personal liberty be reasonable, fair and just, conforming to natural justice, and not arbitrary, fanciful or oppressive.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is correct. II is the reason for I: once the procedure laid down by a law must itself be fair, just and in conformity with natural justice, a law prescribing an arbitrary procedure can be struck down, so Article 21 protects against arbitrary legislative action too (Laxmikanth p.148).
w: Rejected: Statement-II supplies the very test that makes a law open to being struck down, so it does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; Maneka Gandhi required the procedure prescribed by law to be fair, just and reasonable.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; after Maneka Gandhi a law prescribing an arbitrary procedure can be struck down.

questions.q:
Match each clause of Article 19 in List-I with the freedom whose restrictions it governs in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 19(2)
B. Article 19(3)
C. Article 19(4)
D. Article 19(6)

List-II
1. Right to form associations or unions or co-operative societies
2. Right to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business
3. Right to freedom of speech and expression
4. Right to assemble peaceably and without arms
questions.e: Table 8.5 (Laxmikanth pp.142-144): the grounds of restriction on speech and expression are laid down in Article 19(2), on assembly in 19(3), on association in 19(4), and on profession, occupation, trade or business in 19(6); movement and residence are governed by 19(5).
w: 'A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2' swaps A and B: speech is governed by 19(2) and assembly by 19(3).
'A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2' swaps B and C: assembly is 19(3) and association 19(4).
'A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1' swaps C and D: association is 19(4) and profession, trade or business 19(6).

concepts.name: Rights against exploitation, of religion and of minorities
concepts.description: Articles 23 to 30: bans on forced labour and child labour, freedom of religion, and cultural and educational rights.
concepts.idea: Articles 23 to 30 protect people from exploitation and protect religious and cultural freedoms.
concepts.rule: Article 23 prohibits human trafficking and forced labour (begar). Article 24 forbids employing children below 14 in factories, mines or other hazardous work. Article 25 gives every person freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality and health. Article 26 lets religious denominations manage their own religious affairs. Article 27 says no one can be compelled to pay taxes for promoting a particular religion. Article 28 restricts religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained by the State. Article 29 protects the language, script and culture of any section of citizens, and Article 30 gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
concepts.example: A factory cannot employ a 12-year-old to work on hazardous machinery.

questions.q: The State announces compulsory military or national service for all adults of a certain age group, without any additional payment, and a petitioner invokes Article 23. According to the chapter, the State's action is
questions.a: permissible as compulsory service for a public purpose, provided the State does not discriminate on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class
o: permissible as compulsory service for a public purpose, provided the State does not discriminate on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class
impermissible, because Article 23 prohibits every form of compulsory work and has no exception for any public purpose, however important the purpose may be
permissible only if it has been authorised by a proclamation of National Emergency, since Article 23 can be set aside at no other time or for any other purpose
permissible only against citizens, since Article 23 protects non-citizens from compulsory service of every kind and gives citizens no protection at all
questions.e: Article 23 permits the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes, such as military or social service, for which it is not bound to pay; but it may not discriminate on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class (Laxmikanth pp.153-154).
w: The chapter records an exception for public purposes.
The exception does not depend on an Emergency proclamation; it is part of Article 23 itself.
Article 23 is available to citizens and non-citizens alike, and the exception turns on public purpose, not nationality.

questions.q: In 1996 the Supreme Court gave directions on child labour that included a fine on offending employers. Which of the following correctly states it?
questions.a: A fine of Rs 20,000 for each child employed, to be deposited in a Child Labour Rehabilitation Welfare Fund
o: A fine of Rs 20,000 for each child employed, to be deposited in a Child Labour Rehabilitation Welfare Fund
A fine of Rs 2,000 for each child employed, to be paid to the child as compensation for lost schooling
A fine of Rs 20,000 for each factory employing a child, to be deposited in the Consolidated Fund of the State
A fine of Rs 50,000 for each child employed, to be deposited in a National Commission for Protection of Child Rights fund
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.154): in 1996 the Supreme Court directed the establishment of the Child Labour Rehabilitation Welfare Fund, in which the offending employer should deposit a fine of Rs 20,000 for each child employed.
w: The amount is Rs 20,000, deposited in a fund.
The fine is per child employed, not per factory, and goes to the Rehabilitation Welfare Fund.
The fine is not Rs 50,000 and the fund is the Child Labour Rehabilitation Welfare Fund.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Article 26 from Article 25?
questions.a: Article 26 protects denominations collectively; like Article 25 it is subject to public order, morality and health, but unlike Article 25 it is not subject to the other Fundamental Rights provisions
o: Article 26 protects denominations collectively; like Article 25 it is subject to public order, morality and health, but unlike Article 25 it is not subject to the other Fundamental Rights provisions
Article 26 protects individuals rather than denominations, and, like Article 25, it is subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions relating to Fundamental Rights
Article 26 protects the collective freedom of denominations, and, like Article 25, it is subject to the other provisions of Part III but not to public order, morality or health
Article 26 protects individuals rather than denominations, and, unlike Article 25, it is subject to no restriction of any kind whatever
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.155): Article 25 guarantees the rights of individuals while Article 26 protects the collective freedom of religious denominations or their sections; both are subject to public order, morality and health, but Article 26 is not subject to the other provisions relating to Fundamental Rights.
w: Article 26 is for denominations, not individuals, and is not subject to other FR provisions.
Both Articles are subject to public order, morality and health.
Article 26 is for denominations, and it is subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.q: A private school is recognised by the State but receives no aid from it. A student is asked to attend the school's daily prayer. According to Article 28 as explained in the chapter,
questions.a: religious instruction or worship may be offered, but no student can be made to attend without consent (a guardian's, if a minor)
o: religious instruction or worship may be offered, but no student can be made to attend without consent (a guardian's, if a minor)
no religious instruction or worship can be provided at all in the school, since it is an institution recognised by the State and is treated as public
attendance can be required of every student by the school, since the institution is not wholly maintained out of State funds and is privately managed
attendance can be required if the school was established under a trust, whatever the student's or guardian's consent, as the trust exception applies to it
questions.e: Article 28 distinguishes four types of institutions; in institutions that are recognised or receive aid, religious instruction is permitted on a voluntary basis: no person can be required to attend without consent, and the guardian's consent is needed for a minor (Laxmikanth p.156).
w: Complete prohibition applies only to institutions wholly maintained by the State.
Recognised or aided institutions cannot require attendance without consent.
The trust-based exception applies to institutions administered by the State, and consent is still required in recognised ones.

questions.q: A minority educational institution seeks neither recognition nor aid from the State. Which of the following is correct according to the chapter?
questions.a: It is free to administer its own affairs, subject only to general laws such as contract, labour, industrial and tax law
o: It is free to administer its own affairs, subject only to general laws such as contract, labour, industrial and tax law
It is subject to the State's regulation on syllabus, academic standards, discipline, sanitation and the employment of teaching staff
It is free from every law of the land, since Article 30 gives minorities a right placed above general laws
It is not a minority educational institution protected by Article 30, since the protection requires recognition
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.157): the first two types (recognition and aid; recognition only) are subject to the State's regulatory power on syllabus, standards, discipline, sanitation and teaching staff; the third type, which neither seeks recognition nor aid, is free to administer its affairs but subject to general laws such as contract, labour, industrial, tax laws.
w: That regulatory power applies to the first two types.
The Supreme Court summary states there is no reverse discrimination; general laws apply equally (p.158).
The chapter lists three types of minority institution, including the one that seeks neither.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 23:

1. Devadasi practice, slavery and immoral trafficking in women and children are among the forms covered by 'traffic in human beings', along with buying and selling people like goods.
2. 'Begar' means compulsory work without remuneration.
3. A worker who accepts less than the minimum wage out of economic necessity is not in 'forced labour', since force means physical or legal compulsion.
4. A private employer cannot be proceeded against under Article 23, which restrains the State alone.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The chapter's four sub-heads. Statement 2 is correct: A system under which local zamindars sometimes forced tenants to render services without payment. Statement 3 is incorrect: It includes force arising from the compulsion of economic circumstances, such as working for less than the minimum wage. Statement 4 is incorrect: It protects against the State and also against private persons.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 24 and child labour:

1. Article 24 bars children below 14 from work in factories, mines and hazardous activities such as construction work or railway.
2. Article 24 also prohibits the employment of children below 14 in harmless or innocent work.
3. Employing a child below 14 as a domestic servant or in a tea-shop, dhaba or hotel was banned by the government in 2006.
4. The Factories Act, 1948 and the Mines Act, 1952 are among the laws that bar the employment of children below certain ages.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 in any factory, mine or other hazardous activity such as construction work or railway (Laxmikanth p.154). Statement 2 is incorrect: the Article does not prohibit employment in harmless or innocent work (p.154). Statement 3 is correct: in 2006 the government banned child employment as domestic servants and in tea-shops, dhabas and hotels, with prosecution for offenders (p.154). Statement 4 is correct: the chapter lists the Factories Act, 1948 and the Mines Act, 1952 among the statutes that prohibit child employment below certain ages (p.154).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.154
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.154
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.154

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 25:

1. Article 25 freedoms yield to public order, morality, health and the remaining provisions in Part III.
2. Article 25 protects only religious beliefs and doctrines and does not extend to religious practices and rituals.
3. The State may provide for social welfare and reform or throw open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus.
4. The rights are available to all persons, citizens as well as non-citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 25 freedoms are subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III (Laxmikanth p.155). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 25 covers religious practices and rituals as well as beliefs and doctrines (p.155). Statement 3 is correct: the State may regulate secular activity, provide for social welfare and reform, and throw open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes of Hindus (p.155). Statement 4 is correct: Article 25 says 'all persons', so non-citizens are covered (p.155).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.155
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.155
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.155

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about religious denominations and Article 26:

1. The holder of the right under Article 25 is the individual, and under Article 26 it is the religious denomination or a section of it.
2. The Supreme Court held that the Ramakrishna Mission and Ananda Marga are religious denominations within the Hindu religion, but that the Aurobindo Society is not.
3. To be a denomination a group needs doctrines it holds conducive to spiritual well-being, a shared organisation and a name of its own.
4. Article 26 includes the right to own and acquire movable and immovable property and to administer such property in accordance with law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 26 protects collective freedom. Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 3 is correct: Three conditions laid down by the Supreme Court. Statement 4 is correct: Part of Article 26.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 27 and 28:

1. Article 27 forbids the State from spending tax money on the promotion or maintenance of any religion at all, including all religions equally.
2. A fee, unlike a tax, may be levied on religious endowments to meet the expenditure of regulating them.
3. The protection of Article 27 is available to citizens and foreigners alike.
4. Article 28 bars religious instruction altogether in an institution that is run wholly on State money.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The chapter says taxes can be used for the promotion or maintenance of all religions; what is barred is compelling payment for a particular one (p.155). Statement 2 is correct: Stated under Article 27 (p.156). Statement 3 is correct: Table 8.2 lists Article 27 in the column open to both (p.130). Statement 4 is correct: Article 28 (p.156).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.155
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.155
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.155

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 29:

1. The first provision of Article 29 protects the right of an individual citizen, and the second provision protects the right of a group.
2. A State-aided college may not refuse a citizen admission solely because of the applicant's religion, race, caste or language.
3. A candidate who promises at election meetings to protect a language is not guilty of a corrupt practice under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
4. Article 29 protects only religious minorities and gives no protection to linguistic minorities.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The first protects a group's right to conserve its language, script and culture; the second protects the individual's right of admission. Statement 2 is correct: The second provision. Statement 3 is correct: The right to conserve includes the right to agitate. Statement 4 is incorrect: It protects both religious and linguistic minorities.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:

1. Compensation fixed for compulsorily acquiring a minority institution's property must not dilute its Article 30 right, a safeguard inserted in 1978.
2. The Constitution defines a 'minority' as a religious or linguistic group that is numerically smaller than the rest of the population of a state.
3. A minority may educate its children through the medium of its own language as part of Article 30.
4. A minority-run institution cannot be treated worse than others when the State distributes aid.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Added along with the deletion of the property right. Statement 2 is incorrect: The term has not been defined anywhere in the Constitution. Statement 3 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 4 is correct: Third provision.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following principles laid down by the Supreme Court in 2006 in the Malankara Syrian Catholic College judgment:

1. The right of minorities to establish and administer institutions includes the right to choose a governing body in whom the founders have confidence.
2. Article 30 was meant to give minorities a privileged footing over the majority, a kind of reverse discrimination in their favour.
3. The State cannot impose any condition when it gives aid to a minority educational institution, since aid alters its nature.
4. The right is not absolute and does not include the right to maladminister; regulatory measures to maintain standards are allowed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the minority right includes choosing a governing body in whom the founders have confidence (Laxmikanth p.158). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 30 only ensures equality with the majority and gives no reverse discrimination (p.158). Statement 3 is incorrect: aid does not alter the nature of the institution, and the State may impose conditions for proper utilisation of the aid (p.158). Statement 4 is correct: the right is not absolute, does not include a right to maladminister, and allows regulatory measures to maintain standards (p.158).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.158
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.158
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.158

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the rights in Articles 25 to 30:

1. The rights under both Article 25 and Article 26 are subject to public order, morality and health.
2. Freedom of conscience and religion under Article 25 is available to foreigners as well as citizens.
3. Article 29 and Article 30 are listed in the chapter among the rights available only to citizens.
4. Freedom from payment of taxes for the promotion of a religion under Article 27 is available only to citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: both Article 25 and Article 26 are subject to public order, morality and health, though Article 26 is not subject to the other Fundamental Rights provisions (Laxmikanth p.155). Statement 2 is correct: Table 8.2 lists Article 25 among the rights open to foreigners as well as citizens (p.130). Statement 3 is correct: Table 8.2 leaves Articles 29 and 30 in the citizen-only column (p.130). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 27 is open to foreigners as well as citizens (p.130).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.155
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.155
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.155

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the four types of educational institutions in Article 28:

1. A college whose entire cost is borne by the State may not impart religious instruction at all.
2. Religious instruction can be given in a State-administered institution that came into being through an endowment or trust requiring it.
3. In institutions recognised by the State or receiving State aid, no religious instruction can be given in any manner.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Type 1. Statement 2 is correct: Type 2. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is permitted on a voluntary basis. So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about minority educational institutions:

1. Institutions that seek both recognition and aid, and those that seek only recognition, are subject to State regulation of syllabus and academic standards.
2. The institutions that seek neither recognition nor aid are free to administer their affairs, subject to general laws such as contract and tax law.
3. Once a minority institution takes State aid, its character as a minority institution is altered.
4. Unaided minority institutions can appoint teachers by any rational procedure of selection, once the State's eligibility conditions are met.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: First two types. Statement 2 is correct: Third type. Statement 3 is incorrect: It does not. Statement 4 is correct: Fourth principle. So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 25:

1. For Sikhs, carrying a kirpan counts as part of the profession of their faith under an explanation to Article 25.
2. Under Article 25 the State may regulate a secular activity, whether economic, financial or political, that is associated with a religious practice.
3. The second explanation says that Hindus do not include Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: First explanation (p.155). Statement 2 is correct: One of the two permitted State actions (p.155). Statement 3 is incorrect: Hindus include Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists in this context (p.155). So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A fee may be levied on pilgrims for providing special services or safety measures without violating Article 27.
Statement-II: A fee is a payment for a service or for regulation, and is not a tax whose proceeds promote or maintain a religion.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a fee can be levied on pilgrims for special services or safety measures (Laxmikanth p.156). Statement-II is correct: Article 27 prohibits only a tax whose proceeds are for promoting or maintaining a religion, and a fee is a payment for a service or regulation, not such a tax (p.156). II explains I: because a pilgrim fee is not a tax of that kind, charging it does not violate Article 27.
w: Rejected: the link exists; because a pilgrim fee is not a tax for promoting a religion, charging it does not offend Article 27.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; a fee is a payment for a service or regulation and not a tax for religion (p.156).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; the chapter says a fee can be levied on pilgrims for special service or safety measures (p.156).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A linguistic group that forms the majority in a State may also invoke the first provision of Article 29.
Statement-II: Article 29 speaks of 'any section of the citizens', and is therefore not restricted to minorities.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is correct. The Supreme Court held that because of the words 'section of citizens', Article 29 includes the majority as well as minorities (Laxmikanth p.156). So II explains I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; Article 29 says 'any section of the citizens' (p.156).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; the Supreme Court held that Article 29 covers the majority as well as minorities (p.156).

questions.q:
Match each Article in List-I with its distinguishing feature in List-II, as given in the chapter.

List-I
A. Article 25
B. Article 26
C. Article 27
D. Article 28

List-II
1. Collective rights of religious denominations, which yield to public order, morality and health but not to the other Fundamental Rights provisions
2. Bars compelling a person to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion
3. Rights of individuals, which yield to public order, morality, health and also the other provisions relating to Fundamental Rights
4. Completely prohibits religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds
questions.e: Article 25 guarantees the rights of individuals, subject to public order, morality, health and the other Fundamental Rights provisions; Article 26 protects denominations collectively, subject to public order, morality and health only; Article 27 bars compulsion to pay taxes for a particular religion; Article 28 prohibits religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained by the State (Laxmikanth pp.155-156).
w: 'A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4' swaps A and B: Article 25 is individual, Article 26 collective.
'A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2' swaps C and D: Article 27 concerns taxes and Article 28 religious instruction.
'A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4' swaps B and C: Article 26 is the denominations' right and Article 27 the tax rule.

concepts.name: Constitutional remedies and writs
concepts.description: Article 32, Article 226, the five writs and the special status of the right to move the courts.
concepts.idea: Article 32 makes the right to move the Supreme Court a fundamental right, and the courts issue writs to enforce rights.
concepts.rule: Article 32 lets a person go directly to the Supreme Court to enforce a fundamental right, and Dr Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution. High Courts have a similar and wider power under Article 226, which can also be used for purposes other than fundamental rights. The five writs are habeas corpus (produce the person detained), mandamus (a command to perform a public duty), prohibition (stops a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction), certiorari (quashes an order of a lower court or tribunal) and quo warranto (asks by what authority a person holds a public office). Parliament can make the right to move the courts unavailable only as the Constitution provides, such as during a national emergency under Article 359.
concepts.example: A writ of habeas corpus can be filed if a person is held without lawful authority.

questions.q: A contractor with a government department approaches a High Court for a writ of mandamus to compel the department to perform its obligations under a signed works contract. Which of the following is the position according to the chapter?
questions.a: The writ will not be issued, because mandamus cannot be used to enforce a contractual obligation
o: The writ will not be issued, because mandamus cannot be used to enforce a contractual obligation
The writ will be issued, because the department is a public body and mandamus lies against any public body
The writ will be issued only if the department is an inferior court or tribunal, against which mandamus lies
The writ will not be issued, because mandamus can be issued only for the enforcement of a Fundamental Right
questions.e: Mandamus is a command to a public official or public body to perform a public duty; it cannot be issued against a private body, to enforce departmental instruction without statutory force, where the duty is discretionary, to enforce a contractual obligation, or against the President or governors (Laxmikanth p.160).
w: Mandamus against a public body lies for a public duty, not for a contract.
Mandamus may issue against a public official, a corporation, an inferior court or government, but not to enforce a contract.
A High Court can issue writs also for purposes other than Fundamental Rights (p.160), so that is not the reason.

questions.q: A woman is allegedly confined against her will in a private house by a private individual. For her release, a writ petition is filed. Which of the following is correct?
questions.a: Habeas corpus is the right writ, since it can go against a private person who holds another in confinement, and not only against officials
o: Habeas corpus is the right writ, since it can go against a private person who holds another in confinement, and not only against officials
A writ of habeas corpus cannot be issued, because it lies only against public authorities and an arrest by a private individual is outside its reach
A writ of mandamus can be issued, because it directs a private person who has wrongfully confined another to perform his duty of releasing her
A writ of quo warranto can be issued, because it enquires into the legality of her detention and the authority of the person who holds her
questions.e: Habeas corpus ('to have the body of') orders the person who has detained another to produce the body before the court, which examines the legality; it can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals (Laxmikanth p.160).
w: The chapter says it lies against private individuals too.
Mandamus cannot be issued against a private individual or body.
Quo warranto examines a claim to a public office, not detention.

questions.q: A petitioner asks a high court to test, through a writ, the claim of a person to an office. According to the chapter, quo warranto can be issued in which of the following situations?
questions.a: Where the post is a substantive public office, permanent in character, that owes its creation to a statute or to the Constitution
o: Where the post is a substantive public office, permanent in character, that owes its creation to a statute or to the Constitution
Where the office is a ministerial post in a government department, because the salary of the post is paid out of public revenues
Where the office is a private one, such as a company's directorship, provided the petitioner is the person aggrieved by the appointment
Where the appointment is a temporary one made by an administrative order, provided the petitioner is a public-minded person
questions.e: Laxmikanth (p.161): quo warranto ('by what authority or warrant') can be issued only in the case of a substantive public office of a permanent character created by a statute or by the Constitution; it cannot be issued in cases of a ministerial office or a private office.
w: A ministerial office is expressly outside the writ.
A private office is expressly outside the writ, whoever the petitioner is.
A temporary appointment is not a substantive office of a permanent character created by a statute or the Constitution.

questions.q: A lower tribunal is hearing a case over which, in the view of a High Court, it has no jurisdiction, and the final order has not yet been passed. To stop the proceedings, the High Court should issue
questions.a: a writ of prohibition, which is issued before the final order is passed to stop the continuance of proceedings
o: a writ of prohibition, which is issued before the final order is passed to stop the continuance of proceedings
a writ of certiorari, which is issued before the final order is passed to stop the proceedings
a writ of mandamus, which directs the tribunal to decide the case within its own jurisdiction
a writ of certiorari, because it quashes the proceedings of a tribunal as soon as its jurisdiction is doubted, even before any order is passed
questions.e: Prohibition ('to forbid') is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction; it is issued before the final order to stop the proceedings, whereas certiorari is issued after the final order to quash it (Laxmikanth p.161).
w: Certiorari is issued after the final order is passed, to quash it.
Mandamus directs activity; the need here is to direct inactivity.
Certiorari quashes an order already passed (p.161); it is not a writ that halts a tribunal's proceedings merely because its jurisdiction is doubted.

questions.q: Article 32 allows a court other than the Supreme Court to be given the power to issue directions, orders and writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. According to the chapter, who can confer this power, and on which courts?
questions.a: Parliament alone, under Articles 32 and 35; the power does not extend to the high courts, which already hold it under Article 226
o: Parliament alone, under Articles 32 and 35; the power does not extend to the high courts, which already hold it under Article 226
Each state legislature, for the courts in its own state, under Article 226; the power then extends to the high courts of the state as well
The President, by an order under Article 359 during an Emergency; the power then extends to the high courts but not to subordinate courts
Parliament or a state legislature, whichever has the subject in its own list; the power then extends to the high courts too, by the same law
questions.e: Article 32 says Parliament can empower any other court to issue directions, orders and writs, without prejudice to the Supreme Court's own powers; 'any other court' does not include the high courts, because Article 226 already confers the power on them (Laxmikanth p.158-159). Article 35 vests the power to make such a law only in Parliament and not in the state legislatures (p.163).
w: Under Article 35 only Parliament, not a state legislature, can make this law; and the high courts already have the power.
Article 359 deals with suspending the right to move courts in an Emergency, not with conferring writ powers.
Article 35 gives the power to Parliament alone, and the high courts are outside the idea of 'any other court'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the provisions of Article 32:

1. Article 32 itself guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings when a Part III right is infringed.
2. The power of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is not confined to the named writs; it extends to appropriate directions and orders as well.
3. The writs named in Article 32 are habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and injunction.
4. The Supreme Court has ruled that Article 32 is a basic feature of the Constitution, so it cannot be abridged even by a constitutional amendment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: First provision (p.158). Statement 2 is correct: Second provision (p.158). Statement 3 is incorrect: The five writs are habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto; injunction is not among them (p.158). Statement 4 is correct: Stated in the chapter (p.158).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.158
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.158
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.158

questions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning Articles 32 and 226 as sources of writ power:

1. The Supreme Court can issue writs for any purpose, while a high court can issue them only for Fundamental Rights.
2. A writ of the Supreme Court runs against any person or government in India; a high court's writ reaches those within its own territory or, beyond it, only if the cause of action arose within it.
3. A remedy under Article 226 is a Fundamental Right, while a remedy under Article 32 is discretionary.
4. Under Article 226 a high court has a discretion to decline a writ petition.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is the reverse: the Supreme Court only for Fundamental Rights, a high court also for any other purpose. Statement 2 is correct: Territorial jurisdiction differs. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is the reverse: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right and Article 226 is discretionary. Statement 4 is correct: Because a remedy under Article 226 is discretionary.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of habeas corpus:

1. It literally means 'to have the body of', and is an order to the person who has detained another to produce the detained person.
2. A private individual who keeps another in confinement is as much open to this writ as a government officer.
3. A person lawfully committed to custody by a competent court can have the detention examined and ended through this writ.
4. Where a person is held for contempt of a legislature or a court, this writ will not secure release.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The court then examines the cause and legality of detention. Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is not issued where the detention is by a competent court. Statement 4 is correct: One of the listed cases.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of prohibition:

1. Like mandamus, prohibition directs activity on the part of the authority to which it is issued.
2. It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping one it does not possess.
3. It cannot be issued against a purely administrative authority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Unlike mandamus, which directs activity, prohibition directs inactivity (p.161). Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text (p.161). Statement 3 is correct: The chapter says it is not available against administrative authorities (p.161).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.161
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.161
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of certiorari:

1. Like prohibition, it is a jurisdictional writ.
2. Excess of jurisdiction or want of jurisdiction is the ground on which it issues.
3. In the literal sense it means 'to be certified' or 'to be informed'.
4. It is issued before the final order is passed, to stop the further continuance of the proceedings.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: certiorari, like prohibition, is a jurisdictional writ (Laxmikanth p.161). Statement 2 is correct: it is issued on the ground of excess or lack of jurisdiction (p.161). Statement 3 is correct: in the literal sense it means 'to be certified' or 'to be informed' (p.161). Statement 4 is incorrect: certiorari is issued after the final order to quash it; prohibition is the writ issued before the final order to stop the proceedings (p.161).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.161

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of quo warranto:

1. It literally means 'by what authority or warrant'.
2. It can be sought only by a person who claims the office for himself, and not by any other member of the public.
3. It enquires into the legality of the claim of a person to a public office and prevents illegal usurpation of it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: quo warranto literally means 'by what authority or warrant' (Laxmikanth p.161). Statement 2 is incorrect: the writ can be sought by any public-minded person and not necessarily by the aggrieved person (p.161). Statement 3 is correct: it enquires into the legality of a person's claim to a public office and so prevents illegal usurpation of it (p.161).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.161
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.161

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scope of Article 32:

1. Article 32 does not merely confer a power on the Supreme Court, as Article 226 does on a high court, but is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. The jurisdiction is 'wide' because the power is not restricted to orders or directions but also extends to writs of all kinds.
3. A petitioner is not shut out of the Supreme Court merely because another remedy is open to him.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Stated in the comparison with Article 226 (p.160). Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text (p.159). Statement 3 is correct: Because Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, an alternate remedy is no bar (p.159).
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.160
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.160
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.160

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the suspension of the right to constitutional remedies:

1. Article 359 allows the President to suspend only the right to move the Supreme Court, and not the right to move a high court.
2. An order under Article 359 leaves the rights alive on paper and takes away only the means of enforcing them.
3. Even in an Emergency, the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 stays beyond the reach of a Presidential Order since the 44th Amendment.
4. The Presidential Order suspending enforcement is to be laid before each House of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It allows suspension of the right to move any court. Statement 2 is correct: They remain theoretically alive. Statement 3 is correct: Both stay enforceable even during an Emergency. Statement 4 is correct: For approval.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of mandamus:

1. It does not lie against a private individual or body, unless that body has been entrusted with a public duty.
2. It cannot be issued to enforce a departmental instruction that does not have statutory force.
3. It cannot be issued where the duty is discretionary and not mandatory.
4. It can be issued against the President of India and the state governors to compel them to perform their official duties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the chapter lists the private individual or body among the limits on mandamus (Laxmikanth p.160); the settled qualification is that a private body entrusted with a public duty can be reached, which the statement allows for. Statement 2 is correct: a departmental instruction that has no statutory force cannot be enforced by mandamus (p.160). Statement 3 is correct: mandamus does not lie where the duty is discretionary and not mandatory (p.160). Statement 4 is incorrect: it cannot be issued against the President or the governors, though it can be issued against an inferior court, a tribunal, a corporation or the government (p.160).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.160
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.160
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.160

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's and the high courts' jurisdiction over Fundamental Rights:

1. The Supreme Court's jurisdiction in the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is original but not exclusive, being concurrent with that of the high courts.
2. When a Fundamental Right is violated, the aggrieved party has the option of moving either the high court or the Supreme Court directly.
3. Parliament has so far empowered some courts other than the Supreme Court and the high courts to issue writs.
4. Any power Parliament may give another court is without prejudice to the Supreme Court's own writ powers.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 226. Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 3 is incorrect: No such provision has been made so far. Statement 4 is correct: Fourth provision of Article 32. So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about writs:

1. In England they are known as 'prerogative writs', as they were issued in exercise of the prerogative of the King, the 'fountain of justice'.
2. Before 1950 only the high courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras had the power to issue the writs.
3. In England the high courts later issued these writs as ordinary remedies for the settlement of private civil disputes.
4. Where the high court can give relief under Article 226, the Supreme Court expects the petitioner to approach that court in the first instance.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: in England they are called prerogative writs because they were issued under the prerogative of the King, the fountain of justice (Laxmikanth p.159). Statement 2 is correct: before 1950 only the high courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras could issue them, and Article 226 now empowers all high courts (p.159). Statement 3 is incorrect: in England they were extraordinary remedies to uphold the rights and liberties of the British people, not remedies for private civil disputes (p.159). Statement 4 is correct: where a high court can give relief under Article 226, the Supreme Court expects the petitioner to approach it first (p.159). So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 32:

1. Its purpose is to provide a guaranteed, effective, expeditious, inexpensive and summary remedy for the protection of Fundamental Rights.
2. The Supreme Court has been constituted as the defender and guarantor of the Fundamental Rights.
3. It can be invoked merely to test the constitutionality of a legislation even if it does not directly infringe a Fundamental Right.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 is meant to give a guaranteed, effective, expeditious, inexpensive and summary remedy for protecting Fundamental Rights (Laxmikanth p.159). Statement 2 is correct: the Supreme Court is constituted as the defender and guarantor of the Fundamental Rights (pp.159-160). Statement 3 is incorrect: violation of a Fundamental Right is the sine qua non, so Article 32 cannot be invoked merely to test the constitutionality of a law (p.159). So exactly 2 of the 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'All three' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.
'None' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 2 correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The writ of certiorari could initially be issued only against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities, but the Supreme Court later ruled that it can be issued even against administrative authorities affecting the rights of individuals.
Statement-II: Certiorari is issued to a person who has detained another, ordering him to produce the detained person before the court.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct (Laxmikanth p.161). Statement-II is incorrect: that describes habeas corpus; certiorari is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to quash the order passed by the latter.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is not correct; it describes habeas corpus, not certiorari.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.161): initially only judicial and quasi-judicial authorities were reached; it is Statement-II that is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Article 32 can be invoked only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, and not for statutory or customary rights.
Statement-II: A high court under Article 226 can issue writs for the enforcement of an ordinary legal right as well as of Fundamental Rights.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: only the Fundamental Rights can be enforced under Article 32 (Laxmikanth p.159). Statement-II is correct: a high court can issue writs for any other purpose, meaning an ordinary legal right (p.160). Statement-II describes the wider writ power of a high court; it does not give the reason why Article 32 is confined to Fundamental Rights, so it does not explain Statement-I.
w: Rejected: the confinement of Article 32 to Fundamental Rights is a feature of that Article; the wider power of the high court does not cause it.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct; under Article 226 a high court can issue writs for any other purpose too (p.160).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct; Article 32 is confined to the Fundamental Rights (p.159).

questions.q:
Pair each Article in List-I with its subject-matter, as set out in the chapter, in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 32
B. Article 226
C. Article 359
D. Article 13

List-II
1. Writ power of the high courts, which extends also to other purposes
2. Right to constitutional remedies, itself a Fundamental Right
3. Voids any law that conflicts with the rights in Part III
4. Suspension of the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency
questions.e: Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies (p.158); Article 226 is the high courts' writ power, wider than Article 32 (p.160); Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move courts during a national emergency (p.159); Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Part III (p.132).
w: 'A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3' mismatches A, B: Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies (p.158); Article 226 is the high courts' writ power, wider than Article 32 (p.160); Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move courts during a national emergency (p.159); Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Part III (p.132).

'A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4' mismatches C, D: Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies (p.158); Article 226 is the high courts' writ power, wider than Article 32 (p.160); Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move courts during a national emergency (p.159); Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Part III (p.132).

'A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3' mismatches B, C: Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies (p.158); Article 226 is the high courts' writ power, wider than Article 32 (p.160); Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move courts during a national emergency (p.159); Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Part III (p.132).

concepts.name: Limits, emergencies and landmark ideas about rights
concepts.description: Reasonable restrictions, armed forces, the effect of an emergency, the amendment power and the basic structure idea.
concepts.idea: Rights can be limited and amended, but the Supreme Court has held that the basic structure cannot be destroyed.
concepts.rule: Rights come with reasonable restrictions. Article 33 lets Parliament modify these rights for members of the armed forces and similar services. During a national emergency the rights under Article 19 are suspended when the emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression, and the President can suspend the right to move the courts for the enforcement of other rights under Article 359; after the 44th Amendment the rights under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended. Article 368 gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution. In Golaknath (1967) the Supreme Court held that Parliament could not amend fundamental rights, but in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) it held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot change its basic structure.
concepts.example: Article 21 remains available even during an emergency.

questions.q: A state legislature passes a law restricting the right of the members of the state police force to form associations and to attend public meetings, in the interest of discipline. The validity of the law under the chapter is
questions.a: doubtful, since only Parliament, and not a state legislature, can restrict Fundamental Rights of police forces under Article 33
o: doubtful, since only Parliament, and not a state legislature, can restrict Fundamental Rights of police forces under Article 33
sound, because police is a state subject and the state legislature can restrict any right of its own force in the interest of discipline
sound, because a law made for the discipline of the forces, by whichever legislature, cannot be challenged in any court on any ground
doubtful, because the Fundamental Rights of the members of the police force cannot be restricted by any authority, Parliament included
questions.e: Article 33 empowers Parliament (and not state legislatures) to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces, para-military forces, police forces, intelligence agencies and analogous forces, to ensure discipline; a parliamentary law under it cannot be challenged for contravening a Fundamental Right (Laxmikanth p.161). Article 35 also vests such lawmaking in Parliament alone (p.163).
w: The Article 33 power vests only in Parliament.
A law by Parliament under Article 33 is immune from challenge on Fundamental Rights grounds; a state law has no such shield.
Article 33 expressly lets Parliament restrict these rights.

questions.q: Which of the following statements on martial law is correct according to the chapter?
questions.a: It has no express provision and is implicit in Article 34, and its declaration does not by itself suspend the writ of habeas corpus
o: It has no express provision and is implicit in Article 34, and its declaration does not by itself suspend the writ of habeas corpus
Article 352 expressly authorises it, and it can be imposed only on the grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion
Article 34 defines martial law as military rule, and the ordinary courts continue to function during its operation
It is imposed over the whole country at once, and the Supreme Court has held that it suspends the writ of habeas corpus automatically
questions.e: Laxmikanth pp.162-163: martial law is not defined and there is no express provision authorising it, though it is implicit in Article 34; it is imposed in a specific area; it suspends government and ordinary courts; and the Supreme Court held that its declaration does not ipso facto suspend habeas corpus.
w: Those three grounds and the express provision are features of a National Emergency under Article 352, not martial law.
The expression is not defined anywhere in the Constitution, and martial law suspends the ordinary courts.
Martial law applies to a specific area, and does not automatically suspend habeas corpus.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court judgment reversed the earlier decisions in Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh by holding that the Fundamental Rights were given a 'transcendental and immutable' position, so that an amendment Act was a 'law' under Article 13?
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.198: in Golak Nath (1967), where the Seventeenth Amendment Act was challenged, the Court held that Parliament cannot abridge or take away any Fundamental Right, and that an amendment is a law within Article 13.
w: Kesavananda overruled Golak Nath and held Parliament can abridge FRs but not alter the basic structure.
Minerva Mills (1980) invalidated provisions of the 42nd Amendment.
Indira Nehru Gandhi (1975) invalidated a provision of the 39th Amendment about election disputes.

questions.q: In 1990 Parliament places an Act in the Ninth Schedule by a constitutional amendment, and a petitioner challenges it as violating Article 21. According to the Supreme Court's ruling in I.R. Coelho (2007) as given in the chapter, the Act
questions.a: can be challenged, since a law placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 is open to challenge for violating Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 or the basic structure
o: can be challenged, since a law placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 is open to challenge for violating Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 or the basic structure
cannot be challenged, since Article 31B gives every Ninth Schedule law blanket immunity from judicial review, and judicial review is not a basic feature of the Constitution
can be challenged only if it had been placed in the Schedule before 24 April 1973, as laws placed there afterwards are wholly immune from such a challenge in court
can be challenged under Articles 14 and 19 only, because Article 21 cannot be pleaded against any law that has been placed in the Ninth Schedule by an amendment
questions.e: The Court ruled that there could not be blanket immunity: judicial review is a basic feature and cannot be taken away by putting a law in the Ninth Schedule; laws placed after 24 April 1973 (the Kesavananda date) can be challenged for violating Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 or the basic structure (Laxmikanth p.166).
w: That is the literal text of Article 31B, which Kesavananda and Coelho qualified; judicial review is a basic feature.
The cut-off applies the other way: laws placed after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge.
The challenge extends to Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 as well as the basic structure.

questions.q: In Waman Rao (1980) the Supreme Court clarified the temporal reach of the basic structure doctrine. According to the chapter, it applies to
questions.a: constitutional amendments enacted after 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment
o: constitutional amendments enacted after 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment
all constitutional amendments enacted since the Constitution came into force in 1950, with no date as the starting point
constitutional amendments enacted after the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 only, which curtailed judicial review
constitutional amendments enacted before 24 April 1973 only, which alone are open to challenge now
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.199: in Waman Rao (1980) the Supreme Court adhered to the doctrine of basic structure and clarified that it would apply to constitutional amendments enacted after April 24, 1973, the date of the judgment in Kesavananda Bharati.
w: The doctrine is not retrospective to 1950.
The cut-off is the Kesavananda date, not the 42nd Amendment.
Earlier amendments are not reopened; it is later ones that are tested.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 33:

1. Part III can be restricted or abrogated for the armed forces, para-military and police forces and intelligence agencies by a law of Parliament, to secure their discipline.
2. State legislatures may also make laws under it for the police forces of their states.
3. The Police Forces (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1966 and the Border Security Force Act are among the laws made by Parliament under it.
4. Barbers, cooks, carpenters and tailors employed with the forces are, though non-combatants, within the phrase 'members of the armed forces'.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate the rights of the armed, para-military and police forces and intelligence agencies so that they discharge their duties and keep discipline (Laxmikanth p.161). Statement 2 is incorrect: the power belongs only to Parliament and not to state legislatures (p.161). Statement 3 is correct: the chapter names the Police Forces (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1966 and the Border Security Force Act among the laws enacted under Article 33 (p.161). Statement 4 is correct: barbers, cooks, carpenters, tailors and similar non-combatant employees count as 'members of the armed forces' (p.162).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.161
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing martial law and National Emergency, as given in the chapter:

1. Martial law affects only Fundamental Rights, while a National Emergency also affects Centre-state relations, distribution of revenues and legislative powers.
2. Martial law suspends the government and ordinary courts, while a National Emergency continues them.
3. Martial law can be imposed only on three grounds - war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
4. Martial law is confined to a particular locality, whereas a National Emergency proclamation can cover the whole country or just a portion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 8.7 says martial law affects only Fundamental Rights while a National Emergency also affects Centre-state relations, distribution of revenues and legislative powers (Laxmikanth p.162). Statement 2 is correct: martial law suspends the government and ordinary courts, a National Emergency continues them (p.162). Statement 3 is incorrect: war, external aggression and armed rebellion are the three grounds of a National Emergency; martial law is imposed to restore a breakdown of law and order due to any reason (p.163). Statement 4 is correct: martial law is imposed in a specific area, a National Emergency in the whole country or any part (p.163).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.162
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.162
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.162

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 35:

1. Under Article 35 a state legislature may make a law empowering courts other than the Supreme Court and the high courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
2. Parliament alone can make laws prescribing punishment for untouchability and for traffic in human beings and forced labour.
3. Any law in force at the commencement of the Constitution on the matters specified in Article 35 continues in force until altered, repealed or amended by Parliament.
4. Under it Parliament may legislate on matters which would otherwise lie in the State List.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Parliament alone, not the state legislatures, has this power (p.163). Statement 2 is correct: Articles 17 and 23 (p.163). Statement 3 is correct: Third provision (p.164). Statement 4 is correct: For uniformity throughout the country (p.164).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.163
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.163
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.163

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 31A:

1. It saves laws providing for acquisition of estates and four other categories from being challenged under Articles 14 and 19.
2. It saves the covered laws from being challenged under any of the Fundamental Rights.
3. Immunity under Article 31A for a state law depends on the law having been reserved for the President and having received his assent.
4. Its five categories of saved laws include the amalgamation of corporations and the extinguishment or modification of mining leases.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 31A saves five categories of laws, such as acquisition of estates, from challenge under Articles 14 and 19 (Laxmikanth p.165). Statement 2 is incorrect: its protection is limited to Articles 14 and 19, not every Fundamental Right (p.165). Statement 3 is correct: a state law gets the immunity only if reserved for the President and assented to by him (p.165). Statement 4 is correct: the five categories include amalgamation of corporations and extinguishment or modification of mining leases (p.165).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.165
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.165
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.165

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule:

1. In its text, Article 31B protects the acts in the Ninth Schedule from challenge under any of the Fundamental Rights, whether or not they fall in the five categories of Article 31A, which makes it wider than Article 31A.
2. At its creation in 1951 the Ninth Schedule held 13 acts and regulations.
3. Kesavananda Bharati made Ninth Schedule enactments liable to be tested against the basic structure.
4. The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution in 1971, along with Article 31C.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 31B immunises Ninth Schedule laws from all Fundamental Rights, whether or not they fall within the five categories of Article 31A, so its scope is wider (Laxmikanth p.165). Statement 2 is correct: originally, in 1951, the Ninth Schedule held only 13 acts and regulations (p.166). Statement 3 is correct: in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Court held Ninth Schedule laws open to challenge on the basic structure (p.165). Statement 4 is incorrect: the Schedule dates from 1951, while Article 31C was inserted by the 25th Amendment in 1971 (p.166).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.165
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.165
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.165

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 31C:

1. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
2. A law seeking to implement the principles in Article 39(b) or (c) cannot be void on the ground that it contravenes Article 14 or Article 19.
3. In Kesavananda Bharati the Supreme Court declared the provision that no law with a declaration of giving effect to such policy may be questioned in court to be invalid, as judicial review is a basic feature.
4. A state law gets the protection of Article 31C even if it has not been reserved for the President's consideration.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It was inserted by the 25th Amendment Act of 1971. Statement 2 is correct: Chapter text. Statement 3 is correct: The other provision was held valid. Statement 4 is incorrect: No immunity from judicial review unless reserved and assented.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Articles 358 and 359:

1. Article 358 suspends the freedoms of Article 19 for the entire duration of the Emergency, whereas an Article 359 order may last for the whole Emergency or for a shorter period.
2. Article 359 operates in both external and internal emergencies.
3. Article 359 itself suspends the Fundamental Rights automatically from the moment of the proclamation.
4. A Presidential Order under Article 359 may be confined to part of the country, whereas Article 358 applies to the entire country.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 358 suspends the Article 19 freedoms for the whole Emergency, while an Article 359 order may last for the whole Emergency or a shorter period (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 2 is correct: Article 359 operates in both external and internal emergencies (p.264). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 359 only empowers the President to suspend enforcement of rights by an order; it does not suspend them automatically (p.264). Statement 4 is correct: an Article 359 order may be confined to part of the country, whereas Article 358 applies to the whole country (p.264).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.264
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.264
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.264

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the judicial treatment of Fundamental Rights and amendments:

1. In Shankari Prasad (1951) the Supreme Court held that the power under Article 368 includes the power to amend Fundamental Rights, and that 'law' in Article 13 means ordinary laws only.
2. In Sajjan Singh (1964) the Supreme Court reversed its stand in Shankari Prasad.
3. The challenge in Golak Nath was directed at a 1964 amending Act that had placed certain state enactments in the Ninth Schedule.
4. The 24th Amendment Act (1971) amended Articles 13 and 14 to overcome Golak Nath.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Chapter 12. Statement 2 is incorrect: It reaffirmed the stand. Statement 3 is correct: Chapter 12. Statement 4 is incorrect: It amended Articles 13 and 368.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the elements of the basic structure as recorded in the chapter:

1. In Minerva Mills (1980) the Court identified the limited power of Parliament to amend the Constitution, judicial review, and harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
2. In Bhim Singhji (1980) the Court listed federalism.
3. In S.P. Sampath Kumar (1986) the Court listed the rule of law and judicial review.
4. In Central Coal Fields (1980) the Court listed effective access to justice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 12.1 records for Minerva Mills (1980) the limited amending power of Parliament, judicial review, and harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles (Laxmikanth p.201). Statement 2 is incorrect: for Bhim Singhji (1980) the table records the welfare state (socio-economic justice); federalism is recorded against S.R. Bommai (1994) (pp.201-202). Statement 3 is correct: Sampath Kumar (1986) is linked with the rule of law and judicial review (p.201). Statement 4 is correct: Central Coal Fields (1980) is linked with effective access to justice (p.201).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.201
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.201
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.201

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the effect of the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 on the Emergency-time provisions of Articles 358 and 359:

1. Armed rebellion as the ground of Emergency leaves the Article 19 freedoms unsuspended, whereas war or external aggression suspends them.
2. Laws unconnected with the Emergency enjoy no protection from challenge under either Article.
3. The President can still suspend the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 through an order under Article 359.
4. On the cessation of the Emergency, Article 19 automatically revives.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Not for armed rebellion. Statement 2 is correct: Applies to both Articles. Statement 3 is incorrect: He cannot. Statement 4 is correct: Laws inconsistent with it cease to have effect to that extent. So exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'All four' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.
'Only one' miscounts: the statements checked one by one give exactly 3 correct.

questions.q:
